newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close mixed on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close mixed on profit-taking.

text.p: Profit-taking hit Taiwan share prices in late trade on Wednesday, trimming the market's initial gains and leading to a mixed finish despite the overall index climbing to another six-year high.
The weighted index, which had opened at an intra-day high of 8,330.86 points, closed only 8.43 points, or 0.10 percent, higher at 8,255.07.
The close surpassed the 8,246.64 finish on Tuesday and marked the index's highest level since it reached 8,569.55 on May 15, 1990.
Turnover was a frantic T$179.57 billion.
The market, fuelled by expectations of a continuing economic recovery, has soared over 1,400 points in 1997 -- and nearly 400 points in March alone.
"Caution is finally hitting the market after this long period of sharp gains," said Chen Han-chung, analyst for Yungli Securities.
"The market lacks a clear direction, meaning investors are struggling to find bellwether shares and sectors to lead another rally," Chen said.
Fundamental-backed electronics gained 0.63 percent, with chip giant Mosel Vitelic gaining T$3.30 to T$51.50.
"There are not many clear factors guiding individual shares' movements other than an alternating between profit-taking and bargain-hunting," Chen said.
Brokers said they expected the index to remain in a consolidation on Thursday. A 8,200-8,300 range was seen.
